parole.significato: to dawn (to begin to brighten with daylight)
parole.testo: Proto-Finnic *kaja + -staa, probably from Proto-Uralic *kaja (compare Northern Sami guojihit, Erzya каемс (kajems), Eastern Mari кояш (kojaš), Nganasan [script needed] (kou), Kamassian [script needed] (kuja)).

parole.significato: a mid-sized or mid-density mesh or net in a seine
parole.testo: Proto-Finnic *kala- + -in, derived from Proto-Uralic *kala- (“to fish with a net”), whence Estonian kale, Komi-Zyrian кулӧм (kulöm, “10-15 fathom-long net”), Eastern Khanty каләв (kaləw, “net”), Northern Mansi хӯлуп (hūlup, “net”) and Hungarian háló (“net”).

parole.significato: bad, poor, shoddy, no good (of low quality)
parole.testo: kämä- + -(i)nen, probably from dialectal kämä (“hardened, stuck substance; old, worn thing”). SSA considers this word (which has no known cognates) to be of sound-symbolic origin and that kämärä (which is related to Estonian kämar and Ingrian kämärä) is derived from it. parole.significato: cave, (large) pit, cavity
parole.testo: Proto-Finnic *onkë- + -alo, from Proto-Uralic *woŋke (“hole”). Cognate with Karelian onkura, Ludian ongurtta, and Estonian ungas.

parole.significato: calf (back of the leg below the knee)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pohkëda + -e, derived from Proto-Uralic *počka (whence Erzya пукшо (pukšo, “rump, thigh”)). parole.significato: lard, back fat, bacon fat (subcutaneous pork fat)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Has no cognates in the other Finnic languages, but the variant silevä was found in some dialects. Possibly from Proto-Uralic *śilä (“fat”) (compare Central Mansi [script needed] (šilt), Nganasan [script needed] (séla)), although this is not entirely regular. Alternatively, the word might

parole.significato: to examine, investigate, research, search (through), explore
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tutka + -ia, from Proto-Uralic *tuďka (“tip, end”), probably originally meaning "to prod, goad". The original root *tutka can more clearly be seen in tutkain; modern Finnish tutka (“radar”) is a more recent back-formation.

parole.significato: muffled, subdued, muted, dull
parole.testo: Possibly a blend of vaisu + laimea or vaieta + laimea (in the latter case perhaps through the verb vaimeta or vaimentaa, in which case vaimea is a secondary back-formation). parole.significato: Forms lative adverbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-s, either reduced from *-kse (translative ending): *-kse > *-ks > *-s, or alternatively from Proto-Uralic *-s (compare Erzya -с (-s) in эйс (ejs, “into”)).

parole.significato: Forms nouns, indicating resemblance or association.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-us. Probably generalized from -s-derivatives of u-stem nominals (e.g. etu- → edus, palvelu → palvelus), or through the loss of a plain u-derivative from the standard language (e.g. keski- → dial. kesku- → keskus), and thus identical to -us (etymology 1). parole.significato: Forms an adjective from a noun.
parole.testo: Two theories exist: * Of the same origin as the participle ending above (etymology 1), with the same levelling of the weak grade (*-ba). * Alternatively, from Proto-Finnic *-va, from Proto-Uralic *-ŋa.

parole.significato: dry, rocky hill
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kangar, *kankarëh, probably from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*gangaʀ), a later loan from the same source as kangas (“a soil type with moraine”); alternatively possibly from Proto-Uralic *këŋka- (“to climb”) (compare kangertaa). Related to Estonian kangur, Karelian kankareh and Li

parole.significato: to well (up/forth), spring (up/forth) (e.g. of water or some other liquid matter)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kumbut'ak, probably from Proto-Uralic *kumpa- (“to surge, move in waves”). Alternatively, from kummu- + -ta.

parole.significato: mud, (wet) dirt
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kura (“dirt, mud”) (compare Estonian kura), possibly borrowed from Proto-Germanic *gurą or alternatively from Proto-Uralic *kura (“dirt, mud”).

parole.significato: common European adder (Vipera berus, the only natural species of viper in Finland)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *küü (compare Estonian küü), possibly from Proto-Uralic *kije (compare Erzya гуй (guj), Moksha куй (kuj), Hungarian kígyó), or alternatively an old clipping for kyykäärme (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: to discourage, demoralise/demoralize, dispirit, dishearten, push down, demotivate
parole.testo: According to Aikio (2026), from Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare dialectal lantua, lanttua (“to languish, collapse due to exhaustion, pass out”)), from Proto-Uralic *lëmtɜ- (“to stoop down”) (whence also Proto-Samic *luomtētēk (“to lie down and refuse to get up”), Erzya ландямс (lanďams, “to crouch dow

parole.significato: to lower, move down
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *laskëdak (compare Estonian laskma), from Proto-Uralic *lëćke- (compare Erzya ластямс (lasťams, “to saddle”), Moksha ласькомс (laśkoms, “to run”)). parole.significato: gravel, sediment, crushed rock
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mura, probably from the same Proto-Uralic *mura- (“to break”) as murtaa, or alternatively from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Icelandic mor).

parole.significato: young
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *noori (“young”) (compare Estonian noor), probably from either Proto-Uralic *ńëre (“moist, wet; flexible, pliable”) (compare Northern Sami njuoras, Erzya and Moksha нар (nar, “weed, grass”), Udmurt нюр (ńur, “bog, swamp”), Northern Mansi [script needed] (ńār), Hungarian nyirkos, Tu

parole.significato: balcony, loft, gallery
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *parvi, possibly related to parvi (etymology 1), perhaps originally in the sense "group of logs joined together", or from a separate Proto-Uralic root. parole.significato: that (compare tuo, see usage notes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *se, either from Proto-Uralic *śe or Proto-Finno-Permic *śej. For plural forms, see etymology of ne. The variation in inflectional stems (se-, si-, sii-) dates back to at least Late Proto-Finnic; see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.

parole.significato: an open flat area of land: field, yard
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tandër. Equivalent to *tante- + -re. Cognate to Karelian tanner, Karelian tannar, Veps tandar, Veps tandarta (“to tread down”), Veps tandreh, Estonian tanderdada, Estonian tandermik (“playground”), Proto-Samic *tuontër (“a kind of mountain in Lapland”). parole.significato: thwart (seat across a boat on which a rower may sit)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tukto, either from Proto-Uralic *tuktɜ (“cross-beam”) (compare Hungarian tat (“stern (of a ship)”), Komi-Zyrian тік (tik, “cross wood, cross bar”) and Tym Southern Selkup тати (tati, “thwart (of a ship”)), or alternatively borrowed from Proto-Germanic [Term?] (compare Old Norse þo

parole.significato: can, to be able to, to be capable
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voidak, either from Proto-Finno-Permic *wäjä- or from Proto-Uralic *woje-.
